The diff is four files: the three `hits` and one changeset. No file in it implements or enforces the taught rules; the lint, its `os explain` text and the CLI were read on the PR base `4bba8b8f02f`, not reviewed. The changeset is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged. No schema, lint, runtime or CLI file is in the diff; nothing an author can write is newly accepted or refused. Right.
- Public surface: the published skill text of `@objectstack/skills` changes in three rule files. One owner sentence (relationships.md, Computed column) and two pointers; no SKILL.md, no eval, no reference index touched. Right.
- Severity taught: `warning` at both rule ids, never a refusal. Agrees with `packages/lint/src/stored-expression-inputs.ts` (both issues `severity: 'warning'`) and with the card pointer 6837754404. Right.
- Token ceilings: no ceiling file is in the diff, so none moved. `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · workspace` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` concluded success on this head.
- Still in progress when this record was written, so not yet verdicts: `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. The seat reads them before it adopts this record; a text-only diff gives none of them a path to judge, but their conclusions are theirs.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` matches what the diff publishes: teaching text for behaviour that already shipped, no new capability and nothing withdrawn. The package name resolves (`packages/skills/package.json`).

Clause-②: no. Holds: the diff changes no accept set and no served shape. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds for the same reason.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, one owner sentence plus two pointers instead of three full sentences: accepted. The card asks for the content in each place; a pointer to one owner delivers it and the lane does not duplicate rules.
- Deviation, the dashboards existing-rows clause rewritten: judged in ④, holds.
- Deviation, token payment by deleting restating comments and asides: judged in ④, no rule lost.
- Deviation, no eval added: accepted, the order lists it as optional. The card has no eval prompt, so ④ judges the text against the card's ask and the code on `main`.
- Deviations on the PR trailer and commit trailer are process, not contract; not judged here.
- No escalation.

### ④ Design judgment

**skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md** (the owner sentence). Read against `stored-expression-inputs.ts`, `rule-explanations.ts` (both explanations) and `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-expressions.ts` with `packages/objectql/src/stored-expression-backfill.ts`.

- Holds: "keeps what it held at this row's last write" is the lint's own consequence. `record.product.unit_price` is a counted read (one hop through a `lookup` the example declares, not the hop's `id`). The two forward routes, a `formula` (read time, not totallable) and a snapshot a flow on the related object writes, are the finding's first two ways forward, in its words. The command line is the finding's third, flag for flag: `--field` depends on `--object`, `--changed` recomputes differing values, `--apply` writes. `now()`, `today()`, the acting user and `can()` are all counted volatile inputs and "fixed at the write" is the finding's consequence.
- Tried to break it: "It reads only that row" is a rule for the author, not the engine's behaviour (the engine does read one hop, which is why the warning exists); the next clause says what happens when the rule is broken, so the sentence does not mislead. The bullet's standing advice "keep it stored so the parent `summary` can roll it up" does not collide: the example's `amount` reads `record.unit_price`, the line's own column, which Catalog auto-fill copies from the product.
- **should-fix (S1).** "...or is a snapshot a flow on the related object writes; repair drift with `os migrate stored-expressions --object OBJECT --field FIELD --changed --apply`." The nearest reading is that the command repairs the snapshot's drift. It does not: a flow-written snapshot declares no `expression`, and the backfill refuses a `--field` that "is not a stored computed field" before it reads a row. The command repairs one thing only, a stored expression that already reads a related record and was kept, which is the lint's separate third way forward. The sentence has just told the agent not to keep that shape, so the repair clause has no subject. Name the subject, for example "a field left stored: repair its drift with ...". Five tokens of headroom remain in the file; the fix fits or pays in-file.
- nit (N1). The volatile list is a subset: `daysFromNow()`, `daysAgo()` and `hasCapability()` are counted too. The sentence does not claim to be complete and it is the card's own list; the finding names the exact spelling when it fires.
- nit (N2). No remedy is given for a volatile input (the finding says: a `formula` to show the current value, a scheduled flow to keep a stored one current). The card did not ask for it.
- Cuts: the six example comments, the `relatedListTitle` comment, "(the same source the lookup picker uses)", "(ADR-0085)" and the many-to-many comment. Each fact still stands in the file or its named home: the Sort field, Catalog auto-fill and Computed column bullets; the `relatedListTitle` sentence; `objectstack-data/SKILL.md` line 97 for the lookup picker; the heading and the remaining comment for many-to-many. "typeahead" now lives only in `objectstack-ui/SKILL.md`, which is the section this one already defers to. No rule lost.

**skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md.** The `formula` row's added "that reads only its own row (relationships.md → Computed column)" is a pointer to the owner and says nothing the owner does not. It holds. The cut "Source of truth: ...field.zod.ts" has its home at `skills/objectstack-data/references/_index.md` line 13. No rule lost.

**skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md.**

- "existing rows: `os migrate stored-expressions --apply`" is true of `main`: the command exists, its default run (no `--changed`) fills exactly the rows that hold a NULL the expression gives a value, and `--apply` is what writes. It is also the remedy `rule-explanations.ts` gives for this very pair ("until each is written again or `os migrate stored-expressions --apply` fills them"). The dropped "no hosted backfill yet" was stale and is a separate concern the new text does not claim: a save in publish mode or a publish now fills at the change (`protocol-stored-expression-fill.ts`, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`), and the command is for a definition changed in a repository and booted.
- The phrase "computed and stored on write" that `VIRTUAL_FIELD_AGGREGATE_REMEDY` carries is kept. The `days_count` example reads the row's own `date` fields, so it agrees with "from its own row only".
- nit (N3). The clause no longer says the existing rows are empty until filled, so a total reads low; the command's presence implies it. And the command needs the database URL, while a publish-mode save needs nothing; neither is said. Follow-up material, not a defect.
- Cuts: four ADR-0021 asides. Citations, not rules; the heading "Server-side date bucketing ... (ADR-0021)" and the example comment still carry the ADR. No eval `expected_output` names a deleted fact.

Findings: S1 should-fix; N1, N2, N3 nits. No must-fix. S1's fix moves the head and earns a delta review of the Computed column sentence.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

At-tier delta review of `68194c4d` to `34db3fa5` (the head that holds record 6887741759, PASS with S1 should-fix and nits N1 to N3). The delta touches `relationships.md`, `dashboards.md` and the changeset; `field-types.md` is byte-identical to the reviewed base, so its judgment in 6887741759 stands. The PR is still four files: the three `hits` and one changeset. No file in it implements or enforces the taught rules; the lint, its `os explain` text, the CLI and the metadata doors were read on the PR base `4bba8b8f02f`, not reviewed. The changeset is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged. No schema, lint, runtime or CLI file is in the diff. Right.
- Public surface: published skill text of `@objectstack/skills` in two rule files moves again (one owner sentence, one parenthetical, three example comments removed). No SKILL.md, eval or reference index touched. Right.
- Severity taught: `warning` at both rule ids, unchanged from the base and in agreement with `packages/lint/src/stored-expression-inputs.ts`. Right.
- Token ceilings: `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff, so no ceiling moved (relationships 4127, field-types 3208, dashboards 6232). `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · workspace` and `Type Check · debt ledger` concluded success on this head.
- Still in progress when this record was written, so not yet verdicts: `Test Core (1/8)` and `Test Core (2/8)`. The seat reads them before it adopts this record.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` still matches what the diff publishes: teaching text for behaviour that already shipped. The delta rewrote the changeset's prose only; the frontmatter and both declaration lines are unchanged.

Clause-②: no. Holds: no accept set and no served shape changes. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds for the same reason.

The changeset prose now carries the dashboards claim judged in ④ S2 ("they stay NULL until `os migrate stored-expressions --apply` fills them"); it lands in the package CHANGELOG and should follow whatever S2's fix says.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- The dev report's deviations were answered in 6887741759; the delta adds none beyond the three further comment cuts, judged in ④.
- The PR body still describes head `68194c4d` (its What-changes text, its token readings 4122 and 6226, and its "Verification: Head 68194c4d" line). Process, not contract; the tree is what was judged.
- No escalation.

### ④ Design judgment

**skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md.** Read against `stored-expression-inputs.ts`, both entries in `rule-explanations.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-expressions.ts` and `packages/objectql/src/stored-expression-backfill.ts`.

- S1, closed. "...or a snapshot a flow on the related object writes; repair a field left stored with `os migrate stored-expressions --object OBJECT --field FIELD --changed --apply`." The repair clause now has its subject: the stored expression that was kept, which is the lint's third way forward and the only thing the command accepts (the backfill refuses a `--field` that "is not a stored computed field"). It can no longer be read as repairing the flow-written snapshot. Flags agree with the CLI: `--field` depends on `--object`, `--changed` recomputes differing values, `--apply` writes.
- N1, closed. The volatile list against the lint's own sets, member for member: `CLOCK_FUNCTIONS` is `now`, `today`, `daysFromNow`, `daysAgo`, all four named; `PERMISSION_METHODS` is `can`, `hasCapability`, both named; the acting user is named as a kind, which covers its four spellings (`current_user`, `user`, `ctx.user`, `os.user`) without listing them. Nothing named that the lint does not count, nothing counted that the sentence leaves out. `os.org` and `label()`, which the lint excludes, are not named.
- N2, closed with one nit. "a `formula` or a scheduled flow keeps it current" is the finding's own remedy pair, and a scheduled flow is real (`type: 'schedule'` in `flow.zod.ts`, taught in objectstack-automation); an update by id recomputes every stored field of the row.
  - nit (N4). The lint scopes the second remedy: "to keep a stored value current as time passes, recompute it with a scheduled flow". That answers the clock. For the acting user and for `can()` / `hasCapability()` a scheduled write stores the flow's own identity (a schedule run has no trigger user and runs as system), never the reader's; only the `formula` answers those. The sentence attaches both remedies to all four inputs. The finding prints the scoped wording when it fires, and the `formula` half is right for every input, so no author is led to a wrong field. "it" also has no singular antecedent in its own sentence. Prose-face fix or follow-up.
- Tried to break it: "stays a `formula` ... or a snapshot" now shares one verb where the base had "or is a snapshot"; it still reads as two alternatives. The command is spelled without `--yes`, which a non-interactive `--apply` needs; the lint and `os explain` spell it the same way and the CLI answers "Re-run with --yes", so it corrects itself.
- Cuts in this delta, three example comments. `// Delete line items when invoice deleted`: the type table row ("Coupled (cascade delete)") and the Delete Behaviors table ("`cascade` | Delete all child records | Invoice → Line Items") carry it. `// Junction: Project Assignment between project and employee`: the heading "Many-to-Many: Junction Object" and the object's own name and two lookups carry it. `// Self-reference`: the heading "Hierarchical: tree (Self-Reference)" and the type table's `tree` row carry it. No eval or other skill file names any of the three strings. No rule lost.

**skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md.** Not in the delta. Its pointer "that reads only its own row (relationships.md → Computed column)" still resolves to the owner sentence, which still opens with that rule. Holds.

**skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md.**

- **should-fix (S2).** "existing rows stay NULL until `os migrate stored-expressions --apply`". The N3 edit turned a pointer (the base read "existing rows: `os migrate stored-expressions --apply`") into a universal claim, and the claim is false on `main` for two of the three ways a row gets its value:
  - A save in publish mode, a publish and a package publish fill existing rows at the change, not opt-in (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-expression-fill.ts`: `PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name`, `POST .../publish`, `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/publish-drafts`; the answer carries `stored-expression-filled`). `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` says so in the command's own row: the command "is for a definition changed in a repository and booted". On that door no row stays NULL.
  - A row is also filled by its own next write. The platform's wording keeps that half everywhere it states this limit: "hold no value until each is written again or `os migrate stored-expressions --apply` fills them" (`rule-explanations.ts`, and `VIRTUAL_FIELD_AGGREGATE_REMEDY`'s jsdoc). The text on `main` before this PR had it too ("until rewritten").
  - Why it is more than a nit: the published skills also serve agents that author through the metadata door (objectstack-platform teaches `PUT /api/v1/meta/...`), and for a hosted tenant the command is not available at all (it needs the database URL). This PR removed "no hosted backfill yet" because it was stale; the replacement now tells that same reader the rows stay NULL until a command they cannot run, when the door has already filled them. The sentence is right only for a definition changed in a repository and booted.
  - Fix on the prose face, paid in-file (2 tokens of headroom): say which change the command is for, or restore the pointer shape. For example "existing rows a publish did not fill: `os migrate stored-expressions --apply`", or "after a repo change, existing rows stay NULL until rewritten or `os migrate stored-expressions --apply`". The changeset sentence follows.
- "NULL" itself is right for a newly declared field or a former `formula` (the CLI description: "they hold NULL until each row is next written").
- The rest of the bullet is unchanged from the reviewed base: "computed and stored on write" is kept, the `days_count` example reads the row's own fields.

Findings: S1 closed; N1, N2 closed; N3's fix opens S2 should-fix; N4 nit. No must-fix. S2's fix moves the head and earns a delta review of the dashboards parenthetical (and the changeset sentence that repeats it).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:三处教 AI「把 formula 的 `expression` 挪到存储字段上」的技能文字补一句：存储计算字段只读本行。读关联记录的值会停在本行上次写入时(`stored-expression-cross-record-input` 警告),读时钟、当前用户、`can()` 会定格在写入时刻(`stored-expression-volatile-input` 警告),并给出出路。主句在 `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` → Computed column,`field-types.md` 与 `dashboards.md` 各一句指过去;顺手把 dashboards 里「no hosted backfill yet」的过时说法改成「发布没有填充的行用 `os migrate stored-expressions --apply`」。`@objectstack/skills` patch changeset。
- 为什么改：卡 #32703。#32529 / #32554 已让平台在编写时对这两类输入发警告，技能没讲,AI 照写就会先收警告再返工。
- 风险与回滚：只改技能文字，不动 schema 与运行时;token 在同文件内删重复内容付清，未抬任何上限。回滚即还原本 PR。
